entries.intent: Describe applying or pausing the current profile. Remove the unrelated claim that old MacTray is migration-only.
State the UAC requirement and that AppInit is detection-only. Do not advertise internal boot-safety reasoning.
State that the running service applies the profile. Remove verified/broadly safety and marketing language.
Explain that the same-named service has a different configuration and therefore is not changed. Avoid abstract safety claims.
Preserve the degraded-state facts: service running, system-wide application unconfirmed, stop remains available. Remove abstract safe-recovery language.
Use user-facing profile language instead of generation internals. Preserve mismatch, stop availability, and non-normal display status.
Preserve the installed legacy service, simultaneous-injection block, and migration action. Remove verified safety signaling.
Preserve the unexpected MacType/MacTray configuration, non-modification policy, and Windows Services action. Remove verified language.
Preserve unreadable information, unknown service identity, and blocked system changes. Remove internal verified/foreign labels and abstract safety language.
Only state that MacTray in the current user session must exit before using the new service. Remove safety signaling and the unsolicited file-deletion disclaimer.
Preserve the unknown process/session and blocked system changes. Remove abstract safe-verification wording.
Identify old MacTray and state that removal is a separate action after migration. Do not mention verification or safety.
Introduce the ordered migration steps without abstract verified/reversible assurances that duplicate the concrete steps below.
State only that the AppInit state and legacy service configuration are read. Do not describe this as checking, verification, validation, or safety.
State that the legacy service registry and current INI state are recorded and an existing profile file is backed up. Do not call the backup exact, verified, or safe.
State the concrete actions in order: stop the legacy service, copy the current profile to the new service, then install and start the new service.
State the one user-relevant assurance: if migration fails, the services and profile are restored to their previous state. Do not add safety or verification language.
State only that migration to the new service completed. Do not mention verification, validation, checks, or safety.

Use the locale's concise, native software-health status equivalent of Healthy/normal. The adjacent runtime label already says the service is running, so do not translate this as ready, preparation complete, or available.
